Page store cutover plan

This page walks through moving page state into the Go daemon. It uses every kapi preset, so it doubles as the visual reference for the design system. See the risky step before you start, and the repo for context.

Track A, the server in review Flip KAPI_STORE back and restart the daemon.

Nothing here ships until the kapi open command lands on main.

The cutover drops writes for about 30 seconds. Schedule it outside business hours.

Go owns all state. The browser keeps nothing and refetches after any reconnect.

Where the state lives

agent -> page file: writes page file -> daemon: mtime change daemon -> event log: appends daemon -> browser: revision event browser -> daemon: op daemon -> page file: applies event log -> kapi watch: streams

An op from the browser takes this path:

browser daemon store browser -> daemon: POST /p/{id}/ops daemon -> store: Apply(rev, op) store -> store: save revs/N.html store --> daemon: new rev, summary daemon --> browser: 200 {"rev":N} daemon -> browser: revision event

The code

// Source returns the current page source and its revision. func (s *Store) Source() ([]byte, uint64) { s.mu.Lock() defer s.mu.Unlock() if s.rev < 1 && len(s.src) == 0 { return nil, 0 } return bytes.Clone(s.src), s.rev } const maxRevs = 200 // keep the last 200 revisions diff --git a/internal/page/store.go b/internal/page/store.go --- a/internal/page/store.go +++ b/internal/page/store.go @@ -12,7 +12,8 @@ type Store struct { mu sync.Mutex path string - rev int + rev uint64 + mod time.Time src []byte } @@ -88,4 +89,4 @@ func (s *Store) Apply(rev uint64, op Op) (uint64, Summary, error) { if rev != s.rev { - return 0, Summary{}, errors.New("stale") + return s.rev, Summary{}, ErrStale }

Latency so far

Endpointp50 msp99 msNotes
GET /p/{id}/411Full render with CSS
GET /p/{id}/blocks/{block}13One element
POST /p/{id}/ops619Writes the file and a revision slowest

Every op writes the page file and a revision copy, and both are synced to disk before the reply.

Transport options

One long GET per tab. Built into every browser and reconnects with Last-Event-ID.

  • No new dependency
  • Plain HTTP, easy to curl

Two-way, but needs its own reconnect and replay logic.

  • Needs a library or hand-rolled framing

Simplest to build. Adds up to a second of lag and wakes the daemon for nothing.

Steps

Add the page store with revisions under revs/. Switch the daemon to serve rendered pages and single blocks. An agent editing the file mid-request can race a browser op. The store must compare mtimes before it writes. Delete the old static page handler. Should undo cross an agent edit, or stop at it? Write the page store tests Run the cutover on staging

Your call

When should the cutover run? Tonight, 22:00 Saturday morning Who needs a heads-up? Support Sales The on-call engineer Anything else?
